title: Bircher Muesli
subtitle: Swiss overnight oats with grated apple and cream
excerpt: Rolled oats soaked overnight in apple juice with grated apple, toasted hazelnuts, and a spoonful of yoghurt stirred in the morning. The original Swiss breakfast of Maximilian Bircher-Benner.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bircher muesli was developed around 1900 by Swiss physician Maximilian Bircher-Benner as a health food for his sanatorium patients. The original contained primarily apple, oats soaked overnight in water with lemon juice, condensed milk, and hazelnuts. Modern Bircher uses apple juice or milk instead of water, and yoghurt replaces condensed milk. Grating the apple directly into the oats and soaking overnight is the correct method: the apple softens and flavours the oats.

content.text: Grate the apple on the large holes of a box grater directly into the bowl so it does not brown. The apple juice provides natural sweetness; taste before adding honey. The oats will absorb all the liquid overnight and the mixture will be thick.
Combine the rolled oats, apple juice, grated apple, and lemon juice in a bowl. Stir, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stir in the yoghurt. Add a splash of apple juice if the muesli is very thick. Taste and add honey if more sweetness is needed.
Divide into bowls. Scatter with toasted hazelnuts and serve immediately.
